**UK government adds payments innovation mandate to Bank of England remit**

*The UK government is directing the Bank of England to support innovation in payment systems and digital money, marking a shift in how it engages with stablecoins and new payment infrastructure.*

The UK government is directing the Bank of England (BoE) to take on a new responsibility to support innovation in payment systems, including digital money such as stablecoins. The instruction, disclosed on August 27, extends the central bank's role beyond its traditional focus on stability and resilience.

The move follows the Treasury's consultation on modernising payments regulation, which proposed consolidating the Payment Systems Regulator's functions into the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA). Adding an explicit innovation mandate signals that the government wants the BoE to play a more active role in shaping – not just overseeing – how payment infrastructure evolves. It also positions the BoE more directly in the stablecoin regulatory space, where it has until now focused primarily on systemic risk assessment.

The practical effect will depend on how the BoE interprets the mandate alongside its stability objectives. The tension between encouraging new entrants and protecting the integrity of systemically important payment systems has been a recurring theme in the Treasury's broader payments reform agenda.

*Sources: [UK Government tells Bank of England to support innovation in payment systems](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48313/uk-government-tells-bank-of-england-to-support-innovation-in-payment-systems?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra | [UK Government tasks Bank of England to support payment systems innovation](https://www.openbankingexpo.com/news/uk-government-tasks-bank-of-england-to-support-payment-systems-innovation/) — Openbankingexpo | [Government pushes Bank of England to innovate on payments and digital currencies](https://www.cityam.com/government-pushes-bank-of-england-to-innovate-on-payments-and-digital-currencies/) — Cityam*

**Swift extends structured address migration deadline for ISO 20022 messages**

*A number of banks requested more time to move from unstructured to structured postal addresses in cross-border payment messages, prompting a reprieve from the November deadline.*

Swift is extending the deadline for migrating from unstructured to structured postal addresses in ISO 20022 payment messages, after a number of banks requested more time to comply. The original November 2026 cut-off had been set as part of the broader ISO 20022 transition for cross-border payments.

The structured address requirement is one of the more operationally burdensome elements of the migration. Banks must update customer records and payment processing systems to replace free-text address fields with standardised components – town, street, postcode – that enable straight-through processing and reduce manual intervention. Many institutions, particularly mid-tier and regional banks, have struggled to clean legacy data at the pace required.

Swift's decision to accommodate the request reflects a pragmatic judgment that enforcing the deadline rigidly would generate compliance failures rather than better data quality.

*Sources: [Swift accepts request to extend structured address migration for ISO 20022 messages](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48318/swift-accepts-request-to-extend-structured-address-migration-for-iso-20022-messages?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

**Digital payments in Italy more than doubled between 2018 and 2025**

*Rapid growth in electronic payments alongside nascent open banking adoption offers a benchmark for how southern European markets are shifting.*

Banca d'Italia has published data showing that digital payments in Italy more than doubled between 2018 and 2025. The central bank notes that open banking services have grown in recent years, representing what it calls "an innovative component of the payment system" aimed at fostering competition and efficiency.

Italy has historically lagged northern European markets in electronic payment adoption, with cash remaining dominant well into the 2020s. The doubling over seven years suggests a structural shift rather than a temporary pandemic effect, though the base was low. Open banking's contribution remains modest in absolute terms but is growing from a near-standing start.

The data arrives as the European Commission pursues enforcement of the instant payments regulation and the digital euro moves through legislative negotiations. Italy's trajectory matters for both: a market that is digitising rapidly but still has significant cash usage presents both the strongest case for new payment infrastructure and the greatest implementation challenge.

*Sources: [Bank of Italy: Digital payments more than doubled between 2018 and 2025](https://www.agenzianova.com/en/news/bankitalia-i-pagamenti-digitali-sono-piu-che-raddoppiati-tra-il-2018-e-il-2025/) — Agenzia Nova*

**Revolut launches dedicated AI research unit to develop in-house banking models**

*Building proprietary machine learning capabilities rather than relying solely on third-party models, Revolut is joining a small group of European fintechs investing in in-house AI research.*

Revolut has launched a dedicated AI research unit designed to develop and deploy in-house banking models. The initiative, reported on August 27, positions the neobank to build proprietary machine learning capabilities rather than depending entirely on external providers such as OpenAI or Anthropic.

European fintechs have broadly adopted third-party large language models for customer service, fraud detection and operational automation. Revolut's decision to establish a self-contained research function suggests the company sees competitive advantage in owning its AI stack – particularly for tasks involving sensitive financial data where reliance on external model providers raises governance and data residency questions.

The move follows a broader pattern of large digital banks investing in AI beyond simple integration. Lloyds deployed agentic AI for scam detection in the first half of 2025, and Starling has added AI-powered tools to its banking assistant. Revolut's approach is more foundational: building the models themselves rather than layering third-party AI onto existing systems.

*Sources: [Revolut debuts AI research unit to power in-house banking models](https://www.fintechfutures.com/ai-in-fintech/revolut-launches-self-learning-intelligence-engine-to-accelerate-ai-deployment) — FinTech Futures*
